stem: A nurse manager identifies rising burnout, short staffing, unpredictable schedules, and excessive administrative burden on the unit. Which response best reflects NIOSH's systems approach to healthcare-worker wellbeing?

options.A: Offer resilience training while leaving staffing, scheduling, workload, and administrative processes unchanged.
options.B: Focus primarily on individual coping and avoid reviewing work-system causes because operational changes may be disruptive.
options.C: Engage staff in reviewing modifiable work-system drivers and pursue operational improvements in areas such as staffing, scheduling, workload, administrative burden, safety, and support.
options.D: Increase mandatory overtime to fill staffing gaps while expanding mindfulness and other individual wellness resources.

rationale: NIOSH's Impact Wellbeing Guide explicitly uses a systems approach and instructs leaders to go beyond encouraging self-care and individual resilience by focusing on operational-level improvements. NIOSH campaign findings identify systemic drivers such as inadequate staffing, demanding or unpredictable schedules, and excessive administrative work, and emphasize staff involvement and two-way communication. Therefore, reviewing and changing modifiable work conditions with staff best reflects the approach; individual wellness resources may complement but should not substitute for system-level improvements.
educational_objective: Address healthcare-worker burnout with a systems approach that engages staff and targets modifiable operational drivers rather than relying primarily on individual resilience interventions.
source_organization: CDC, National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH)
source_version_date: Impact Wellbeing Guide page 2024-09-16; NIOSH Publication 2024-109 revised 2024-07
source_locator: Impact Wellbeing Guide → 'Key principles' (Use a systems approach; Build trust) and Action 1 'Review Your Hospital's Operations'; Campaign Insights → systemic factors at the root of staff burnout.
source_claim_supported: NIOSH directs leaders to go beyond individual resilience toward operational improvements, review hospital operations, involve staff through two-way communication, and address systemic burnout drivers including staffing, demanding schedules, and excessive administrative work.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care activity statements, printed p. 7: participate in performance/quality improvement, manage conflict, utilize resources for quality care; Appendix A Management concepts/collaboration as applicable.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — systems improvement, staff support, and care-delivery operations

source_original.stem: A nurse manager sees rising burnout, short staffing, unpredictable schedules, and excessive administrative burden. Which intervention best reflects NIOSH's systems approach to worker wellbeing?

options.A: Offer resilience training while leaving staffing levels, workload, schedules, and administrative processes unchanged.
options.B: Focus on individual coping and avoid reviewing work-system causes because organizational changes may be disruptive.
options.C: Review operations with staff and address modifiable drivers such as staffing, workload, scheduling, administrative burden, safety, and support.
options.D: Increase mandatory overtime to fill staffing gaps while expanding mindfulness and other individual wellness resources.

source_original.rationale: NIOSH's Impact Wellbeing approach explicitly moves beyond placing the burden on individual resilience. Hospital leaders should examine and improve workplace operations, including staffing and workload, schedule control, administrative burden, safety, communication, and access to support. Individual self-care can complement but not replace system-level improvement.
source_original.source_detail: CDC/NIOSH Impact Wellbeing Guide — systems approach: address organizational drivers such as staffing, workload, schedule control, administrative burden, safety, leadership and access to support rather than relying only on individual resilience. Current NIOSH Impact Wellbeing guidance; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; Assignment, Delegation and Supervision; prioritization/continuity/client rights as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the systems-versus-individual construct and key. Tightened option C to NIOSH's operational-improvement and staff-engagement language and avoided implying that every listed intervention is a universal mandate. Verified the current Guide and its July 2024 revised publication.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Healthcare worker wellbeing — systems-level management response
audit_findings.currentness: Guide page dated September 16, 2024; publication revised July 2024; currentness rechecked 2026-08-16.
audit_findings.exact_locator: Key principles, Action 1, and Campaign Insights directly support systems-level operational review and staff involvement.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final wording says pursue improvements in areas 'such as' the documented drivers, avoiding conversion into mandatory universal interventions.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because it relies on individual resilience while leaving identified operational drivers unchanged.
distractor_audit.B: Directly conflicts with NIOSH systems approach.
distractor_audit.D: Adds a staffing practice likely to worsen the identified scheduling/workload problem while still relying on individual wellness resources.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C addresses the system-level root drivers identified in the stem.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are management responses; the key is not identifiable by an unrelated clinical detail.
audit_findings.blueprint: Fits Management of Care through operational/quality improvement and resource use.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Adversarial review confirmed the item tests systems approach rather than claiming NIOSH mandates a particular staffing ratio or schedule.
